summary: a liquid's viscosity at another temperature, by the Arrhenius form, from a reference point and an activation temperature

inputs.name: reference_viscosity
inputs.meaning: the viscosity at the reference temperature

inputs.name: reference_temperature
inputs.meaning: the temperature the reference viscosity holds at

inputs.name: activation_temperature
inputs.meaning: the activation energy of viscous flow over the gas constant; a property of the liquid, bound to a row with its own source

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.meaning: the temperature the viscosity is wanted at

outputs.name: solvent_viscosity_at_run_temperature
outputs.meaning: the viscosity at the wanted temperature

validity: a simple liquid over a temperature span where one activation temperature holds; every coefficient is an input, so the skill holds none

source.citation: the Arrhenius (Andrade) form of the temperature dependence of a liquid's viscosity
source.locus: viscosity = A * exp(B / T), written relative to a reference point; the coefficients are inputs with their own sources

note: An example of a value skill that gives a correlation. It holds no coefficient: a correlation with fitted coefficients carries them as read from its source, with the locus, and a worked case the source states.
